text:
B: Alright! How you doing?
A: Hello, hello! I'm fine, thank you. I'm Marijke. That's a funny name for you, it's Dutch. I'm from Holland but I live in Kent forever.
B: Zain, from Bolton. Marijke, have I said that right?
A: Close enough. Everybody here says Marika. I gave up correcting in about nineteen eighty-five.
B: Ha, fair. You had that football mug in your photo? No, sorry, that were me.
A: Yes, that was yours! I liked it. Bolton Wanderers. My husband Keith watches all the football, all weekend.
B: Who's he support?
A: Gillingham, sort of. Mostly he watches whatever is on.
B: Respect. I'm a season ticket man in spirit, go to a handful of games with my cousins. What do you do, then?
A: I'm a carer, mornings. I go to people's houses, wash, dress, breakfast, tablets. Done by eleven.
B: That's good, that. Proper important job. My mum worked in a school canteen, the old dears there were like that, looked after everyone.
A: Ha, maybe I'll do dinner ladies next. What about you?
B: Electrician. EV chargers, rewires, all that. I'm going self-employed in a couple of years. Got it all planned in my head, van, logo, the lot.
A: Ooh, a businessman. Can you come and look at my kitchen light? It flickers.
B: Could be the fitting, could be a loose connection. Get someone out, don't leave it, mind.
A: Keith says it's fine. Keith says everything is fine.
B: Ha, every bloke says that. Have you been back to Holland lately? I've always wanted to go to Amsterdam, look at the old buildings.
A: Once a year, to my sister. We drive and take the ferry. But I'm not from Amsterdam, near Arnhem. Amsterdam is all tourists.
B: Fair enough. I'm planning Japan, me. Been watching vlogs for months. Tokyo, Kyoto, the temples, the food. Found some decent flight deals as well.
A: Japan! Too far for me. I've done my moving, I came to England, that's enough.
B: Ha, that's a big move, to be fair.
A: It was. What else, erm... my sister sends me stroopwafels. You know them? Like a biscuit with syrup.
B: Yeah, had them in Istanbul, weirdly, at the airport. They're mint.
A: Mint, yes. I keep them in a tin, I don't give the grandkids too many.
B: You've got grandkids?
A: Three. Every weekend, chaos. I make the dinner, shepherd's pie, Dutch mash.
B: Dutch mash? What's that?
A: Stamppot. Potatoes with kale, sausage. Nothing spicy, I can't do spicy.
B: My mum'd have a field day with you. She puts chillies in everything.
A: I'd pick them out, sorry.
B: Ha, she'd be offended. Oh, I think the timer's going.
